title: Issue of Debentures
outcomes: Define a debenture under section 2(30), list its features and distinguish debentures from shares.
Classify debentures by security, convertibility, permanence, negotiability and priority.
Journalise issue of debentures at par, discount or premium and redeemable at par or premium, including issue by instalments and oversubscription.
Account for debentures issued as collateral security (both methods) and for consideration other than cash.
Write off discount or loss on issue by the straight-line and outstanding-balance methods.
Record debenture interest with tax deducted at source.

meta.exam_tip: The six issue/redemption combinations and the discount write-off table are favourites for 5–6 mark questions; Loss on Issue of Debentures appears whenever redemption is at a premium.

concepts.title: Meaning of a debenture
body: Companies supplement share capital by borrowing through debentures. A debenture is a written acknowledgement of debt issued by the company, setting out the terms for interest and repayment of principal.

Section 2(30): the term covers debenture stock, bonds and every other instrument by which a company acknowledges a debt, whether it creates a charge on the company's assets or not. So debentures may be secured or unsecured.

Where a charge is created, the bond describes the charge and the assets; a charge is valid only when registered with the Registrar. For secured (mortgage) debentures a debenture trustee is usually appointed to protect the holders. No company may issue debentures carrying voting rights (s. 71(2)).
concepts.analogy: A debenture is a formal IOU that a company hands to thousands of lenders at once — each piece has the same terms and can be passed on to someone else.
concepts.work: Debt covenants, charge filings with the Registrar and trustee agreements are checked by auditors and lenders' advisers whenever a company issues secured debentures.

concepts.title: Features of debentures
body: It is a document evidencing a loan to the company.
Interest is at a fixed (coupon) rate on specified dates and is payable whether the company earns a profit or not.
The principal is repaid on a stated future date, or converted into shares or other debentures as per the terms.
It may be backed by a charge on the company's assets, or be unsecured.
It is usually transferable and can be bought or sold on a stock exchange at a price above or below face value.
concepts.analogy: Like a fixed deposit made with a company instead of a bank — fixed interest on fixed dates and a fixed maturity date.
concepts.work: Treasury teams track interest dates and maturity of each debenture series; missing an interest date is a default that can trigger action under s. 71.

concepts.title: Debentures versus shares
body: Status: debenture holders are creditors; shareholders are owners.
Voting: debenture holders cannot vote; shareholders vote and control the company.

Return: debenture interest is at a fixed rate and payable even in a loss year — a charge against profit and deductible for tax. Equity dividend varies with profits (preference dividend is fixed) and is an appropriation of profit, not deductible.
Kinds: debentures come in many kinds (secured/unsecured, redeemable/irredeemable, registered/bearer, convertible/non-convertible); shares are only equity and preference.
Presentation: debentures under long-term borrowings; shares under shareholders' funds — share capital.

Other: debentures can be converted as per terms and cannot be forfeited; shares can be forfeited for unpaid calls. Debenture holders get their money back on maturity and are paid before shareholders on winding up; equity is repaid only on liquidation (preference shares may be redeemed earlier).
concepts.analogy: A shareholder is a partner in the restaurant who shares in good and bad nights; a debenture holder is the bank that lent for the kitchen and expects its EMI whatever the takings.
concepts.work: Choosing between debt and equity funding (cost, tax shield, control, risk) is a classic advisory question CAs answer for clients.

concepts.title: Types of debentures
body: By security: secured debentures carry a charge — fixed (on specific assets, which cannot be sold without the holders' consent) or floating (on all assets, present and future, generally); unsecured or naked debentures carry no charge and are riskier for investors.
By convertibility: convertible (fully or partly, into equity after a period, at par, premium or discount) or non-convertible (repaid as per terms).
By permanence: redeemable (repayable as per terms, e.g. after 7 years) or irredeemable / perpetual (repaid only on liquidation).

By negotiability: registered (names recorded in the register of debenture holders; transfer needs a transfer deed as per the Act) or bearer (transferable by mere delivery; interest paid to whoever holds the coupon).
By priority: first mortgage debentures (paid first out of the charged property) and second mortgage debentures (paid after the first).
concepts.analogy: Secured debentures are a loan against your car (the lender can take the car); naked debentures are a personal loan (only your promise).
concepts.work: Credit-rating agencies and investors price debentures differently by security and priority — the type decides the coupon a client must offer.

concepts.title: Issue of debentures — instalments, oversubscription and the accounts used
body: Debentures can be paid in full with the application or in instalments (application, allotment, calls). A separate application account is kept for each class (e.g., 12% Debenture Application A/c), and on allotment its balance is transferred to the Debentures Account.
Oversubscription is handled as for shares: refund to rejected applicants; excess from pro-rata applicants adjusted towards allotment.

Debentures are always credited at face value. Premium on issue → Securities Premium. Discount on issue → Discount on Issue of Debentures (debit). Premium payable on redemption → Premium on Redemption of Debentures (credit, a liability).
concepts.analogy: Whatever price the debenture is sold at, the "label" on the Debentures Account is always its face value — the difference goes to a side account.
concepts.work: In practice most debentures today are issued fully paid on application through private placement; the instalment entries still matter for exams and older issues.

concepts.title: The six issue–redemption combinations
body: Issued at par / discount / premium and redeemable at par: Bank Dr (cash), [Discount on Issue Dr], To Debentures, [To Securities Premium].
Redeemable at a premium: the redemption premium is a known future liability, so it is recorded at issue — Loss on Issue of Debentures Dr, To Premium on Redemption of Debentures.
Issued at a discount and redeemable at a premium: Bank Dr, Loss on Issue Dr (discount + redemption premium), To Debentures, To Premium on Redemption.

Issued at a premium and redeemable at a premium: Bank Dr, Loss on Issue Dr (redemption premium), To Debentures, To Securities Premium (issue premium), To Premium on Redemption. Redemption at a discount is rare in practice.
concepts.analogy: If you promise to repay ₹110 for every ₹100 borrowed, the extra ₹10 is a cost you have already committed to — so it is booked on day one.
concepts.work: Effective-interest computations for bond pricing start from exactly these components — issue price, coupon and redemption premium.

concepts.title: Debentures as collateral security
body: Collateral security is a secondary security given in addition to the main (primary) security, which the lender can realise only if the loan is not repaid.

A company may hand its own debentures to a bank as collateral for a loan or overdraft. If the loan is repaid, the debentures come back; if not, the lender becomes a debenture holder with full rights. Interest is payable only on the loan, not on the debentures.

Method 1: no entry; a note under the loan states that it is secured by the issue of debentures as collateral. Method 2: Debenture Suspense A/c Dr, To Debentures A/c; in the balance sheet the suspense balance is deducted from the debentures. On repayment of the loan, the entry is reversed.
concepts.analogy: Like giving your landlord a signed but undated cheque as a back-up: it is used only if you fail to pay the rent.
concepts.work: Auditors confirm with the bank that debentures held as collateral have not been invoked, and check the disclosure so readers are not misled into thinking there is double borrowing.

concepts.title: Debentures for consideration other than cash; treatment of discount and loss
body: Debentures can be issued to a vendor for land, machinery or a business: Sundry Assets Dr, To Sundry Liabilities, To Vendor; then Vendor Dr, To Debentures (and To Securities Premium, or with Discount on Issue Dr). Number of debentures = purchase consideration ÷ issue price (face value, face value + premium, or face value − discount).

Discount (and loss) on issue is a capital loss, amortised over the period from issue to redemption: if redeemed in one lot after a fixed period — equally every year (straight line); if redeemed in instalments — in the ratio of debentures outstanding each year. Entry: Profit and Loss Dr, To Discount (or Loss) on Issue of Debentures.

Section 52 also permits writing off such discount or loss against securities premium. The unwritten-off balance is shown as other non-current / current assets depending on when it will be written off. (AS 16 allows discounts related to borrowings to be amortised over the loan period.)
concepts.analogy: If you borrow ₹100 but receive only ₹96, the ₹4 is extra interest in disguise — so it is spread over the years you use the money.
concepts.work: Amortisation schedules for debenture discount are recomputed by auditors every year; a common error is writing off the whole discount in the year of issue.

concepts.title: Interest on debentures and TDS
body: Interest is calculated at the coupon rate on the face (nominal) value, not on the issue price, and is a charge against profit.

The company deducts tax at source as per the Income-tax Act and pays interest net of tax. Entries: Debenture Interest Dr, To Debenture Holders (gross due); Debenture Holders Dr, To TDS Payable, To Bank (payment); TDS Payable Dr, To Bank (deposit with Government); at year end Profit and Loss Dr, To Debenture Interest.
Interest accrued and due or accrued but not due at the balance sheet date is shown under other current liabilities.
concepts.analogy: The company acts like an employer deducting tax from salary: it pays the lender the net amount and sends the tax to the Government.
concepts.work: TDS compliance (deduction, deposit and quarterly returns) on debenture interest is checked in tax audits; delays attract interest and disallowance.

solution.title: Rule of thumb
solution.text: Debentures are always credited at face value (₹10,00,000). Issue premium → Securities Premium; issue discount → Discount on Issue; redemption premium → Premium on Redemption (credit) with an equal amount added to Loss on Issue (debit).

illustrations.title: Debentures payable in instalments, oversubscribed
illustrations.q: Kavach Ltd invited applications for 20,000 12% debentures of face value ₹100 at ₹95 (5% discount), redeemable at par: ₹40 on application and ₹55 on allotment. Applications were received for 26,000 debentures; applications for 2,000 were rejected and the rest were allotted pro rata, the excess application money being adjusted on allotment. All money due was received. Journalise.

Being application money transferred on allotment of 20,000 debentures, excess adjusted and balance refunded

Being balance allotment money received

solution.title: Working
solution.text: Pro-rata applicants applied for 24,000 and got 20,000; excess 4,000 × ₹40 = ₹1,60,000. Allotment due ₹11,00,000 − ₹1,60,000 = ₹9,40,000 received. Debentures credited ₹8,00,000 + ₹12,00,000 = ₹20,00,000 (face value); discount ₹1,00,000.

checks.label: Excess on pro-rata applicants adjusted to allotment

illustrations.title: Writing off discount — one lot vs instalments
illustrations.q: (a) Diya Ltd issued 50,000 debentures of ₹100 at ₹97, redeemable at par after 5 years. (b) Ira Ltd issued 1,20,000 debentures of ₹50 at ₹48, one-fourth redeemable at the end of each year for 4 years. Compute the discount to be written off each year.

solution.text: (a) Discount = 50,000 × ₹3 = ₹1,50,000. Redeemed in one lot, so written off equally: ₹30,000 a year for 5 years.
(b) Discount = 1,20,000 × ₹2 = ₹2,40,000. Redeemed in instalments, so written off in the ratio of debentures outstanding: 60 : 45 : 30 : 15 lakh = 4 : 3 : 2 : 1.

solution.text: Half-yearly interest = ₹10,00,000 × 10% × 6/12 = ₹50,000; TDS ₹5,000; net ₹45,000. Charged to profit and loss for the year ₹1,00,000.
The March TDS is deposited in April of the next year (shown as TDS payable under other current liabilities at year end). TDS rate is assumed for practice.

jobs.title: Booking a private placement of NCDs
jobs.role: Finance executive in an unlisted manufacturing company
jobs.situation: The company has privately placed 2,000 non-convertible debentures of ₹1,00,000 each at ₹98,500, redeemable at par after 3 years in one lot. The CFO asks for entries and the amortisation plan.
steps: Record the issue: Bank Dr ₹19.70 crore, Discount on Issue Dr ₹30 lakh, To NCDs ₹20 crore.
Prepare a straight-line schedule: ₹10 lakh a year for 3 years (one-lot redemption).
Check whether the board wants to use securities premium (s. 52) instead of profit and loss.
Classify the unamortised discount: the part to be written off within 12 months as current, the rest non-current.
Diary the interest dates and TDS deposit dates.
jobs.takeaway: Every debenture issue needs an amortisation schedule from day one; the classification of the unamortised balance changes each year.

jobs.title: Spotting double-counted borrowings
jobs.situation: A client's draft balance sheet shows a bank loan of ₹50 lakh and also 9% debentures of ₹60 lakh issued to the same bank as collateral, both added into long-term borrowings, and it has provided debenture interest of ₹5.4 lakh.
steps: Read the loan sanction letter: the debentures are collateral security only.
Explain that the company owes only the loan; showing both doubles the borrowing.
Propose presentation: either a note under the loan (Method 1) or debentures less Debenture Suspense (Method 2).
Reverse the ₹5.4 lakh interest on the debentures — interest is payable only on the loan.
Re-check debt–equity and interest cover after the correction.
jobs.takeaway: Collateral debentures are a contingent arrangement, not a second loan.

mcqs.q: As per section 2(30), a debenture includes:
options: Debenture stock, bonds or any other instrument evidencing a debt, whether or not it creates a charge
Only secured instruments evidencing a debt
Equity shares with a fixed dividend
Only instruments listed on a stock exchange
mcqs.explain: The definition is inclusive and covers secured and unsecured instruments.

mcqs.q: Which statement about debenture holders is correct?
options: They are creditors and have no voting rights
They are owners and vote at general meetings
They receive interest only when there are profits
Their debentures can be forfeited for unpaid calls
mcqs.explain: Debenture holders are lenders; s. 71(2) bars voting rights; interest is payable irrespective of profit; debentures are not forfeited.

mcqs.q: Debentures that are transferable by mere delivery are:
options: Bearer debentures
Registered debentures
Mortgage debentures
Convertible debentures
mcqs.explain: Bearer debentures are negotiable instruments; registered ones need a transfer deed.

mcqs.q: A charge that covers all the assets of a company, present and future, is a:
options: Floating charge
Fixed charge
Second charge
Collateral charge
mcqs.explain: A fixed charge attaches to specific assets; a floating charge generally covers all assets including future ones.

mcqs.q: 8,000 debentures of ₹100 are issued at ₹98 and redeemable at ₹105. Loss on Issue of Debentures is:
6,000 debentures of ₹100 are issued at ₹103 and redeemable at ₹107. Securities Premium is credited with:
options: Nil
mcqs.explain: Only the issue premium ₹3 × 6,000 goes to Securities Premium; the ₹7 redemption premium goes to Premium on Redemption with a matching Loss on Issue.

mcqs.q: Premium on Redemption of Debentures Account is shown in the balance sheet as:
options: A liability (non-current until the year of redemption)
Part of reserves and surplus
A deduction from debentures
Income in the statement of profit and loss
mcqs.explain: It is an amount payable to holders at redemption — a liability.

mcqs.q: A loan of ₹8,00,000 is secured by 10,000 10% debentures of ₹100 each issued as collateral. Annual interest payable at 12% on the loan and nil on debentures equals:
mcqs.explain: Interest is payable only on the loan: 8,00,000 × 12%.

mcqs.q: Under Method 2 for collateral debentures, the entry is:
options: Debenture Suspense A/c Dr, To Debentures A/c
Debentures A/c Dr, To Bank Loan A/c
Bank A/c Dr, To Debentures A/c
No entry is ever passed
mcqs.explain: The suspense account offsets the debentures in the balance sheet.

questions.q: On 1 April 2026, Rhea Ltd issued 1,00,000 debentures of face value ₹100 at 4% below par, redeemable at par by five equal annual drawings on 31 March each year starting 31 March 2027. Show the discount to be written off each year. What would the yearly write-off be if the debentures were redeemable in one lot after 5 years?

model.text: If redeemed in one lot after 5 years, the discount is written off equally: ₹4,00,000 ÷ 5 = ₹80,000 a year.

checks.label: If redeemed in one lot after 5 years: yearly write-off

remarks: Many divide the discount equally even though redemption is by instalments.
mistakes: Using the debentures redeemed (not outstanding) as the ratio.
Rounding so that the total does not equal the discount.
tips: Show the outstanding amount for each year in a table and add a total row.

questions.q: Distinguish between debentures and shares (any four points).

head: Basis
Debentures
Shares
rows: Fixed interest, payable even in a loss year — charge against profit, tax-deductible
Dividend — appropriation of profit; equity rate varies
Can be forfeited for unpaid calls
Repaid on maturity; paid before shareholders on winding up
Equity repaid only on winding up, after creditors

remarks: Points must contrast both sides; one-sided statements get half marks.
mistakes: Saying debenture interest is an appropriation of profit.

questions.q: Arya Ltd obtained a loan of ₹6,00,000 from a bank and issued 7,000 10% debentures of ₹100 each as collateral security. Explain the meaning of collateral security and show how the debentures will appear in the balance sheet under both methods. Is any interest payable on these debentures?

model.text: Collateral security is an additional (secondary) security given to a lender besides the primary security; it is used only if the borrower defaults.
Method 1: No entry. Under Long-term borrowings: "Bank loan ₹6,00,000 (secured by issue of 7,000 10% debentures of ₹100 each as collateral security)".

entries.narr: Being 7,000 debentures issued as collateral security for the bank loan

model.text: Method 2 presentation under Long-term borrowings: Bank loan ₹6,00,000; 10% Debentures ₹7,00,000 less Debenture Suspense ₹7,00,000 = Nil.
No interest is payable on the collateral debentures; interest is paid only on the loan of ₹6,00,000.

remarks: Many candidates add ₹7,00,000 to borrowings — the company has borrowed only ₹6,00,000.
mistakes: Providing interest on the collateral debentures.
Showing Debenture Suspense as an asset.
tips: Answer both methods side by side and end with the interest point.

viva.q: What is a debenture? State its main features.
viva.model: Under section 2(30), the term debenture covers debenture stock, bonds and every other instrument by which a company acknowledges a debt, whether or not it creates a charge on the company's assets. Its features: it is evidence of a loan to the company; it carries interest at a fixed rate on fixed dates, payable whether or not there is profit; the principal is repaid on a specified date or converted into shares; it may be secured by a charge or unsecured; and it can usually be traded on a stock exchange. Debentures cannot carry voting rights.

points.pt: An instrument evidencing a debt / loan to the company (s. 2(30)), with or without a charge
Fixed rate of interest, payable irrespective of profit
Repaid on a specified date or converted; may be secured or unsecured; no voting rights

viva.q: Give four differences between debentures and shares.
viva.model: Debenture holders are creditors of the company, while shareholders are its owners. Debenture holders have no voting rights; shareholders vote. Debenture interest is a charge against profit, payable at a fixed rate even in a loss year, while dividend is an appropriation of profit. Debentures are shown under long-term borrowings, shares under shareholders' funds. Debentures cannot be forfeited, but shares can, and on winding up debenture holders are paid before shareholders.

points.pt: Debenture holders are creditors; shareholders are owners

viva.q: What is meant by issue of debentures as collateral security, and how is it shown?
viva.model: Collateral security is a secondary or additional security given to a lender besides the main security. When a company issues its own debentures as collateral security for a loan, the lender can use them only if the loan is not repaid. Interest is payable only on the loan, not on these debentures. One method is to pass no entry and only mention the fact below the loan in the balance sheet. The other is to debit Debenture Suspense Account and credit Debentures Account, and show the suspense balance as a deduction from the debentures.

viva.q: Debentures are issued at a discount and are redeemable at a premium. What entry is passed at the time of issue?
viva.model: Bank Account is debited with the cash received, and Loss on Issue of Debentures Account is debited with the total of the discount on issue and the premium payable on redemption. Debentures Account is credited with the face value, and Premium on Redemption of Debentures Account is credited with the premium payable on redemption, which is a liability.

Loss on Issue of Debentures debited with discount + redemption premium
Debentures credited at face value
Premium on Redemption of Debentures credited (a liability)
kw: premium on redemption|redemption premium|premium payable on redemption|premium payable

viva.q: How is discount on issue of debentures written off?
viva.model: The discount is spread over the life of the debentures. If the debentures are redeemed in one lot at the end of a fixed period, it is written off equally every year, which is the straight line method. If they are redeemed in instalments, it is written off in the ratio of the debentures outstanding in each year, so that years using more of the borrowed money bear more of the discount. The entry is Profit and Loss Account debited and Discount on Issue of Debentures credited; the unwritten-off balance is shown as a non-current or current asset.

viva.q: How is interest on debentures recorded when tax is deducted at source?
viva.model: When interest falls due, Debenture Interest Account is debited and Debenture Holders Account credited with the gross interest. On payment, Debenture Holders Account is debited, TDS Payable is credited with the tax deducted and Bank with the net amount. When the TDS is deposited, TDS Payable is debited and Bank credited. At the year end, interest is transferred to the Profit and Loss Account, because it is a charge against profit.

cases.title: Shaurya Infra Ltd — a ₹50 lakh debenture issue
cases.case: On 1 April 2026, Shaurya Infra Ltd issued 50,000 9% debentures of ₹100 each at ₹95, redeemable at ₹104 at the end of 5 years in one lot. The issue was fully subscribed and the money received in full on application. Interest is paid yearly on 31 March, and tax is deducted at source at 10%. The company has a securities premium balance of ₹1,00,000 and decides to write off the loss on issue first against securities premium (as allowed by s. 52) and the rest equally over the 5 years.

mcqs.q: What amount is debited to Loss on Issue of Debentures Account?
At what amount is Premium on Redemption of Debentures credited?
mcqs.explain: Premium payable on redemption ₹4 × 50,000 = ₹2,00,000 — a liability until redemption.

mcqs.q: How much loss is written off to the statement of profit and loss each year?
mcqs.explain: Loss ₹4,50,000 − securities premium ₹1,00,000 = ₹3,50,000, spread equally over 5 years = ₹70,000 a year.

mcqs.q: How much cash is paid to debenture holders as interest on 31 March 2027?
mcqs.explain: Gross interest = 9% × ₹50,00,000 (face value, not issue price) = ₹4,50,000; TDS 10% = ₹45,000; net cash ₹4,05,000.

summary: Debenture (s. 2(30)): instrument evidencing a debt, secured or not; no voting rights (s. 71(2)).
Features: fixed interest regardless of profit, repayment/conversion on a date, may carry a charge, tradable.
Types: secured (fixed/floating) or naked; convertible or not; redeemable or perpetual; registered or bearer; first or second mortgage.
Debentures always credited at face value; issue premium → Securities Premium; discount → Discount on Issue; redemption premium → Premium on Redemption (liability) with Loss on Issue (debit).
Collateral: no entry (note) or Debenture Suspense Dr / Debentures Cr; interest only on the loan.
Discount/loss written off: equally (one-lot) or in outstanding ratio (instalments); may be set off against securities premium (s. 52).
Interest on face value; TDS deducted; transferred to P&L as a charge.
remember: Loss on Issue = discount on issue + premium on redemption.
Interest is on face value, not issue price.
Collateral debentures do not increase borrowings.
traps: Writing off the whole discount in year 1.
Calling debenture interest an appropriation of profit.
